Validation of sustained tokens/sec mapping to reserved GPUs
notes:
Summary: Orthus makes autonomous material-handling robots for cold-chain warehouses. Need deterministic inference for closed-loop control (sub-200ms per decision) and high-volume telemetry embeddings for fleet analytics. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for on-prem deployment.

POC & benchmarks:
- 2026-02-25: Intro call (Jordan + Priya) w/ CTO (M. Alvarez). CTO emphasized: 'we need hard guarantees; cannot have soft best-effort for production control loops.'
- 2026-03-01: Initial throughput benchmark run (POC config #1) captured at edge gateway; results: sustained ~5,200 tokens/sec aggregate across 8 concurrent robots using gpt-like 7B variant, p95 latency 95ms but p99 spikes to 220ms under synthetic burst. (drive: throughput-bench-results-20260305.csv)
- 2026-03-05: Deep technical call with runtime team (Priya, Redwood infra engs) to align on measurement method and KV cache pinning. Fireflies: ff-20260305-throughput-bench.
- 2026-03-10: Legal & security questionnaire submitted; ISO27001 and on-prem KMS integration are must-haves.

Throughput guarantee asks (customer side):
- Minimum sustained guaranteed throughput: 5,000 tokens/sec (account-level) measured as 1-minute rolling average at the service egress point.
- Concurrency cap: guarantee up to 50 concurrent inference sessions with 512-token horizons per session without degradation beyond SLO.
- Burst policy: allow 2x burst (10,000 tokens/sec) for up to 10 minutes per hour without pre-provisioned additional GPUs; additional burst above that should be possible via on-demand capacity at defined burst rate price.
- Deterministic tail latency: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 250ms for per-token generation on committed pool.
- Mapping to reserved GPUs: Orthus needs a clear table that maps committed GPU count (A100-equivalent) to sustained tokens/sec and concurrency. They want the math (batching assumptions, typical sequence lengths, KV cache hit rate) spelled out.

Redwood negotiation positions / open items:
- Redwood provided baseline mapping: 4x A100 -> ~6k sustained tokens/sec under current model (7B) with expected 20-30% headroom for batching improvements.
- Redwood asks to define objective measurement: tokens/sec measured at Redwood ingress or Orthus edge? Redwood proposes measurement at service edge with shared logs and daily report.
- SLA credit model options presented: (a) service credit % of monthly invoice for missed tokens/sec guarantee windows, (b) tiered credit based on duration of degradation. Orthus prefers hard credits + capped liability.
- Burst policy proposal: free bursts up to 1.5x for 5 minutes/hour; extended bursts bill at pre-negotiated burst rate or consume burst credits from monthly committed pool. Orthus pushing for longer free bursts (10 min) due to shift changes in warehouses.
- Concurrency isolation: Redwood can offer a dedicated concurrency pool (isolated slots on reserved GPUs) for guaranteed control-loop sessions; cost premium TBD. Orthus wants at least 30 isolated slots guaranteed.

Technical clarifications requested by Orthus:
- How does Redwood account for batching when measuring per-account tokens/sec vs multi-tenant dedicated pool?
- Do model fallbacks (to a smaller quantized variant) affect SLA counting? Orthus wants fallbacks allowed only for non-control loops; control-loop calls must never be downgraded.
- Prewarm and KV cache pinning: Orthus will pin common prefixes (telemetry header + policy prompts) and expects cache hit-rate guarantees during sustained windows.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: p99 spikes during node draining / autoscaling. Mitigation: Redwood proposed prewarming and staggered node replacement for Dedicated pools; also a canary fallback policy to smaller model for analytics calls only.
- Risk: Burst costs become unpredictable. Mitigation: agree on monthly burst credit bucket and explicit overage pricing formula in SOW.

Commercial asks:
- Commit: initial 12-month Dedicated contract with 4x A100-equivalent reserved, option to scale to 8x after 3 months if POC validated.
- Pricing: orthus requested blended committed rate that includes limited burst credits.

Open legal / procurement items:
- Add explicit measurement specification into SLA (where tokens/sec counting occurs, how batching attribution is allocated).
- Liability cap and service credits clarified for sustained vs transient breaches.

Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-13: Redwood infra to deliver finalized throughput-to-GPU mapping table (action: Priya).
- 2026-03-16: Draft SLA with measurement appendix to legal (Jordan to coordinate).
- 2026-03-20: Orthus legal to return comments; aim to finalize commercial SOW week of 2026-03-23.

Notes tone/remarks: Orthus is very pragmatic — wants the numeric guarantees and the measurement axis in writing. Prefer short, precise SLA language. They repeatedly stated: 'We can tolerate a fallback for analytics, but not for closed-loop decisions.' Keep canary/fallback segregation explicit in proposals.
